title: Das Nachleben der neulateinischen Literatur
bookshelves: Category: Biography, Literature and Literary studies
summary: Early modern Latin literature and culture are often understood primarily in terms of the reception of antiquity. In doing so, it is often overlooked that this literature and culture also developed a life of their own. This volume brings to the fore, for the first time, the hitherto little-researched topic of the later reception of Neo-Latin literature, thereby providing a foundation for further studies. It is aimed at an interdisciplinary readership interested in the transition from the early modern period to the modern era from a philological and cultural-historical perspective. The focus is on receptions in vernacular languages following the widespread decline of Latin literature and culture in the 18th century. The thesis is that themes, concepts, forms and practices which first appeared in, or in connection with, Neo-Latin literature also played a significant role in the modern era from the 19th to the 21st century.
